title: Screen Gems Appoints YouTube Veteran Fede Goldenberg to Lead New Genre Label, THR Reports
body:
Sony Pictures has appointed longtime digital‑media executive Federico “Fede” Goldenberg to take the helm of its genre‑film subsidiary Screen Gems, signaling a bold shift toward a more data‑driven, platform‑savvy approach to mid‑budget horror, thriller and action titles. Goldenberg, who spent the past decade rising through the ranks at YouTube, will replace Ashley Brucks, who is departing the post to focus on a producing deal with the studio’s broader film operations. The move marks the first time a senior YouTube leader has been tapped to run a traditional Hollywood studio label, and it underscores Sony’s intent to blend streaming‑era insights with its long‑standing expertise in theatrical releases.

Goldenberg’s résumé reads like a roadmap of the digital revolution that reshaped content consumption. Starting as a product manager for YouTube’s advertising products, he later oversaw creator partnerships, audience development, and monetization strategies that helped the platform become the world’s largest video destination. Under his stewardship, YouTube expanded its original programming slate and refined algorithms that surface niche content to massive audiences—a skill set that aligns closely with the needs of a label like Screen Gems, which thrives on low‑budget, high‑impact genre films that can find cult followings both in theaters and online.

The departure of Ashley Brucks, who guided Screen Gems through a recent string of modest box‑office successes such as “Reside” and “The Nightwatcher,” is being framed as a natural evolution. Brucks will remain at Sony Pictures in a producer capacity, focusing on developing franchise‑ready properties that can leverage the studio’s global distribution network. Industry observers note that Brucks’ move could free her to concentrate on larger‑scale projects while allowing Goldenberg to inject fresh perspectives into the label’s day‑to‑day operations.

Analysts see the appointment as part of a broader trend among legacy studios to import digital expertise in order to better predict audience tastes and optimize release strategies. With streaming platforms now dominating viewership metrics, the ability to parse real‑time data and tailor marketing pushes has become a competitive advantage. Goldenberg’s background in algorithmic recommendation systems could enable Screen Gems to more precisely target the hyper‑engaged fan bases that fuel the success of horror and thriller franchises, from social‑media buzz to grassroots fan‑generated content.

The decision also reflects Sony’s ongoing recalibration of its mid‑budget slate after a series of mixed results in the post‑pandemic market. While blockbuster tentpoles continue to command the lion’s share of resources, genre films remain a reliable profit center when produced efficiently. By placing a digital‑native leader at the helm, Sony hopes to tighten the feedback loop between audience reaction, promotional spend, and creative development, potentially shortening the turnaround time from greenlight to release and reducing the risk of costly misfires.

Looking ahead, Goldenberg’s first challenge will be to demonstrate that data‑centric decision‑making can coexist with the creative instincts that have historically defined Screen Gems’ brand. Early moves are expected to include a review of the label’s upcoming slate, the integration of YouTube‑style audience testing, and the exploration of cross‑platform release windows that blend theatrical runs with strategic streaming premieres. If successful, the experiment could become a blueprint for other studios seeking to modernize their genre divisions, marrying the immediacy of digital analytics with the timeless appeal of horror, thriller and action storytelling.
